# Calendar shows a second demonstration: a year at a glance

## Context

Calendar is a group of its own in the examples list and shows one card on `dev` `78013b10fc`. #21140's target keeps it at one for the cut, because depth is an engine gap first (the event model has no recurrence and no resources), and names one lead that needs no engine work: "a card that opens on the month or year view". The renewed `calendar/basic` opens on the month, so the year is the view no card shows. No leaf was filed for the lead.

## The Problem

A group with one card reads as a component the engine has only a sample of. The calendar has a year view, and a visitor cannot see it without finding the view switch inside the one example.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/calendar/view/YearComponent.mjs`: the year view.
- `examples/calendar/basic` is the renewed base example (a team's month, relative to today); the week and day views carry an all-day row since #20883.
- Whether the year view marks days that have events, and how it holds at 390×844, is not driven on `dev` yet.

## The Fix

Step one is a drive of the year view at both sizes, with the result on this ticket. Then one new example in its own folder that opens on the year: the same kind of believable team data as the base example, generated relative to today, the days with events marked if the view can mark them, and a click on a day opening that day or week. One line on the first frame says what to try. If the year view cannot carry this at 390×844, the example offers the month there and the ticket says so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The result of the drive is on this ticket before the build.
- [ ] The example opens on the current year with today marked, and a click on a day opens that day's events.
- [ ] Its data is generated relative to today, in the example.
- [ ] No console error, at 1440×900 and at 390×844, in every theme the base example offers.
- [ ] A second record in Calendar with a caption in the visitor's words and a cover from its first frame (through `neomjs/pages`).
- [ ] The look: the first frame at both sizes and the frame after a click on a day, Neo Dark, on the pull request, read cold by the reviewer's seat.

**Publication (added 22 Nov, the same for every leaf of this wave).** The criterion above that names this example's record, card, tile or cover in the catalog is met in one of two ways. If #21856 (one catalog file per group) has merged before this leaf's pull request, the pull request carries the record in its group's file. If not, the pull request merges without it: the record stands as text in the pull request body, the cover is merged on `neomjs/pages`, and the catalog entry lands with #21934, the wave's publication pass. Either way this leaf closes with its example.

## Out of Scope

Recurrence, resources and any other change to the event model (investigation 4 of #21140's roadmap). A renewal of `calendar/basic`.

## Avoided Traps

- **The base example with another start view.** A second card that differs by one config value is a twin; this one has its own data and its own action.

## Timeline

- 2026-11-22T11:37:21Z @neo-fable-clio cross-referenced by #21140
### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-11-22T11:58:08Z

**Drive of the year view**, on `dev` `50fcfc526c`. I opened `examples/calendar/basic`, switched to Year, in headless Chromium on a light theme.

- **1440 × 900:** the 12 months sit in four columns on one screen. Days with events carry `neo-events-low` / `-medium` / `-high` (9 / 6 / 5 cells, because the base data only fills the weeks around today), and today carries `neo-today`. No console error.
- **390 × 844:** one month per row, 390 px wide, with no horizontal scroll. The view opens on January, so today (November) is ten months down. No console error.
- **A click on a day does nothing** at either size: `YearComponent` listens only to its nav buttons and the wheel.

So the build:
1. **The day click goes into `YearComponent`.** A click on a date cell sets the calendar's date and opens its day view when the calendar offers one. Every calendar's year view lacks this, not only the example's. It is a view interaction and leaves the event model alone (your Out of Scope).
2. **The year view carries a phone** if the example opens scrolled to the current month there. The month fallback is not needed.
3. **The example's data spans the year**, generated relative to today, so the marks show the team's year and not one week of it.
